name: Brittany Quansah
missingPieces: D1 only catalogues 6 of 10 findings (missing hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019, no token expiry, stored XSS cookie beacon, path traversal, cookie Secure/SameSite); evidence lines are paraphrased not quoted with line numbers or capture timestamps; decoy mis-identified. D2 has no timestamps, no verbatim PoC payloads, no CVSS vector strings (only 3 bare scores), no naira impact, no assumptions. D3 remediation ordered by severity not effort, detection stopgaps lack exact field and false-positive rate, decoy wrong. D4 under 300 words, NDPA not cited by section, not all four prompts clearly owned.
feedback: D1: You correctly classified five of the core bugs (SQL injection A03/CWE-89, MD5 storage A02 where CWE-327 is an acceptable variant of CWE-916, JWT alg:none A07 where CWE-345 is acceptable for CWE-347, open redirect A01/CWE-601, and XXE A05/CWE-611), and that classification work is the strongest part of the submission. What held this row down is that your evidence column is prose description, not the quoted source line or the capture timestamp the key asks for, so each finding earns about half. You also catalogued only six of the ten findings, missing the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019, the absent token expiry, the stored XSS with the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443, the path traversal at files/?path=/etc/passwd returning root:x:0:0:, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite. Your decoy is wrong: you named developer comments as the safe construct, but the real decoy is the b64url helper or the HS256 verify branch that uses hash_equals, which is constant-time and therefore sound, and the lesson is that alg:none and the hardcoded secret are the real bugs while that one branch is safe. D2: You named 312 affected customers and the data fields, which is good, but the chain is four generic steps rather than the ordered hops three through eight reconciled to capture lines (recon 02:14:08, SQLi 02:15:31, bulk PII 02:16:04 with 312 rows, stored XSS 02:18:47, open redirect 02:21:13, file read 02:24:02), and you provided no verbatim payloads such as admin' OR '1'='1. Your CVSS is three bare scores with no vector strings and no justifying sentence, where SQLi should read AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1 with A:N because the bypass does not touch availability, and you gave no naira impact, where balances up to about 950k NGN across 312 customers sum to tens of millions tied to the BoltCash launch. D3: Your executive summary and threat model are present and readable, but the summary does not land on a customers-and-naira headline, the decoy is repeated incorrectly, and critically you state the remediation is ordered by risk severity rather than effort, which caps that row because the key wants effort-to-risk ordering with the earliest-break fix called out. Your detection stopgaps are generic WAF and logging with no exact log field and no false-positive rate. D4: You cite ISC2 Canon I by number in a load-bearing way, which is correct, but the piece is about 285 words and under the 300 floor, you reference the NDPA without the section, where you needed section 40 (notify NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk) tied to the 312 customers, and the four prompts (the journalist, what you put in writing, the colleague evidence, the one action regardless of the manager) are not all clearly answered in your own voice. I looked for a defensible way to round this up, but with only six findings, no quoted evidence lines, no CVSS vectors, and no naira figure, the work does not support a higher mark. The single most important fix is to quote the actual source line or capture timestamp for every finding and complete the catalogue to all ten, because proof beats the label and a partial catalogue cannot earn a passing D1.
